primary.note: Sole accent; raw form is #49b4c4 (sea-cyan). ~6.94:1 on primary-foreground.

display.purpose: Hero KPI numbers and page/view titles in Newsreader serif, tabular figures. Reads as a chart sounding.

title.purpose: CardTitle in Newsreader 500, sentence case, leading-none.

body.purpose: Inter 400 for dense UI text, tables, descriptions.

label.purpose: Letter-spaced uppercase Inter (the .font-cond hook) for KPI plate labels, nav group headers, readout captions.

mono.purpose: JetBrains Mono tabular for vessel names, versions, shadow prices, readout values.

shadows.name: overlay-modal
shadows.purpose: Modal only (shadow-2xl); the sole heavy shadow.

motion.name: fade-in-up
motion.purpose: Content region enters on tab change (panels rise like a depth reading).

motion.name: focus-ring
motion.purpose: Cyan focus-visible ring; reduced-motion guarded globally.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only cyan-filled control; every action button on screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: hsl(188 51% 53%); color: hsl(200 68% 10%); padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color .14s ease, transform .07s ease, opacity .14s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: hsl(188 51% 53% / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0.5px) scale(0.994); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(73 180 196 / 0.8); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: hsl(209 42% 20%); color: hsl(205 22% 93% / 0.9); padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid hsl(208 55% 25% / 0.8); border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color .14s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: hsl(208 44% 23%); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(0.5px) scale(0.994); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field; mono for numeric/CSV entry.
components.css: .ds-input { background: hsl(210 73% 13% / 0.5); color: hsl(205 22% 93%); padding: 6px 12px; border: 1px solid hsl(208 55% 25% / 0.8); border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; outline: none; transition: border-color .14s ease; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: rgb(6 182 212 / 0.5); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid rgb(73 180 196 / 0.8); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Marine Scheduler reads like a modern bathymetric chart rendered on a screen: a deep-ocean field, hairline graticule lines dividing every readout, and a single cyan depth-contour accent that carries all action. Everything sits on one continuous dark ground with panels raised by a half-step of lightness rather than by shadow. This is the Bathymetric Blue world, which fully replaced an earlier Signal Code system built on nautical signal flags; the flag metaphor is gone, though the primitives still carry their old export names to stay drop-in. The system is desktop-first and unapologetically data-dense; legibility at density is the governing constraint, so contrast is engineered, not decorative.
keyCharacteristics: One deep-ocean ground; panels lift by tonal step, never by heavy shadow.
A single cyan accent for every action and active state.
Serif (Newsreader) for titles and hero numbers; the numbers read as chart soundings.
Hairline borders function as chart graticule; KPI strips are one panel split by gap-px.
Status color routes only through a muted sea palette (ok / warn / bad), never raw Tailwind hues.

rules.name: The One Contour Rule
rules.body: Cyan is the only accent. If a control needs to signal primary action or active, it uses cyan; nothing else in the system is allowed to. Secondary actions stay neutral (bg-muted).

rules.name: The Muted-Sea Rule
rules.body: Status meaning routes only through ok / warn / bad (and destructive for alert chrome). Never reach for raw Tailwind emerald, red, amber, or green.

rules.name: The Sounding-Number Rule
rules.body: Big numbers are serif (Newsreader) and tabular; small figures inline in text are mono (JetBrains). A KPI value is never set in Inter.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Titles and labels are sentence case; only the micro-label tier is uppercase, and only via letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Tonal-Lift Rule
rules.body: A panel is distinguished from its background by a lightness step and a hairline border, not by a shadow. Reserve box-shadow for true overlays (modal, toast).

rules.name: The Graticule Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px chart rulings, not containers. KPI plate strips are a single panel divided by gap-px over a bg-border/40 seam.

dos: Do carry every action and active state on cyan (hsl(188 51% 53%)); primary buttons are bg-primary + text-primary-foreground.
Do set hero KPI numbers and titles in Newsreader serif with tabular figures, and inline figures in JetBrains Mono.
Do build KPI strips as one bordered panel divided by gap-px, not as separate floating cards.
Do route all status through ok / warn / bad utilities and flag severity with a Pennant.
Do keep corners at 6px (rounded-md) and borders hairline; lift panels by tonal step, not shadow.
Do use sentence case for titles and reserve uppercase for the letter-spaced micro-label tier.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color for actions; if it acts, it is cyan.
Don't use raw Tailwind emerald / red / amber / green for status — use the muted sea palette.
Don't put drop shadows on resting surfaces; shadows belong only to overlays (modal, toast).
Don't set a KPI value in Inter, or a body label in serif.
Don't revive the retired Signal Code flag metaphor; the marks are chart soundings and ticks now, despite the legacy SignalFlag filename and exports.
Don't spend sea sand (#d8c4a0) anywhere but the LOAD stop marker — it is the system's only warm note.
